latin: TE igitur, clementissime Pater, per Jesum Christum Filium tuum Dominum nostrum, supplices rogamus ac petimus, uti accepta habeas, et benedicas, hæc dona, hæc munera, hæc sancta sacrificia illibata, imprimis quæ tibi offerimus pro Ecclesia tua sancta catholica: quam pacificare, custodire, adunare, et regere digneris toto orbe terrarum: una cum famulo tuo Papa nostro N. et Antistite nostro N.
notes: Two-line drop T with `E` in capitals, given here as TE. The book prints NO cross signs in this Latin column: the three the Roman rite marks over `hæc dona, hæc munera, hæc sancta sacrificia` are absent from both columns of this printing. `imprimis` here with m, against `inprimis` with n at seq 8; both are transcribed as printed.

latin: et omnibus Orthodoxis, atque Catholicæ et Apostolicæ Fidei Cultoribus.
notes: A separate printed block, opening lower-case, as the sibling English row does.

latin: Memento Domine famulorum famularumque tuarum N. et N.
notes: The book prints no comma after `Memento`.

latin: Et omnium circumstantium, quorum tibi fides cognita est, et nota devotio, pro quibus tibi offerimus: vel qui tibi offerunt hoc sacrificium laudis, pro se, suisque omnibus: pro redemptione animarum suarum, pro spe salutis et incolumitatis suæ: tibique reddunt vota sua æterno Deo, vivo et vero.
notes: Runs over the page break xxxiii/xxxiv, breaking at `pro redemp-` / `tione`.

latin: COMMUNICANTES, et memoriam venerantes, inprimis gloriosæ semper Virginis Mariæ, Genitricis Dei et Domini nostri Jesu Christi: sed et beatorum Apostolorum ac Martyrum tuorum, Petri et Pauli, Andreæ Jacobi, Joannis, Thomæ, Jacobi, Philippi, Bartholomæi, Matthæi, Simonis et Thadæi: Lini, Cleti, Clementis, Xysti, Cornelii, Cypriani, Laurentii, Chrysogoni, Joannis et Pauli, Cosmæ et Damiani, et omnium Sanctorum tuorum: quorum meritis precibusque concedas, ut in omnibus protectionis tuæ muniamur auxilio. Per eumdem Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.
notes: DIFFERS FROM 1962 PRACTICE: this Canon has NO clause naming Saint Joseph. The list passes straight from `Jesu Christi` to `sed et beatorum Apostolorum`, the clause `sed et beati Joseph, ejusdem Virginis Sponsi` having been inserted into the Canon by later legislation, after this printing and after the 1962 typical edition itself was declared; what is being said here is that the text differs from 1962 practice, not that it differs from the 1962 book, and no dated decree is asserted from this witness. `COMMUNICANTES` is set in small capitals and given here in capitals. The book prints `inprimis` with n here and `imprimis` with m at seq 2; `Thadæi` is its spelling; and no comma follows `Andreæ`, which stands at a line end.

latin: Hanc igitur oblationem servitutis nostræ, sed et cunctæ familiæ tuæ, quæsumus Domine, ut placatus accipias: diesque nostros in tua pace disponas, atque ab æterna damnatione nos eripi, et in Electorum tuorum jubeas grege numerari. Per Christum Dominum nostrum. — Amen.
notes: `Hanc igitur` is set in italic, the rest in roman. Runs over the page break xxxiv/xxxv, breaking at `ut placatus accipias:` / `diesque`. An em rule stands between `nostrum.` and `Amen.`, as printed. `Amen.` italic.

latin: Quam oblationem tu Deus in omnibus, quæsumus benedictam, adscriptam, ratam, rationabilem, acceptabilemque facere digneris; ut nobis Corpus et Sanguis fiat dilectissimi Filii tui Domini nostri Jesu Christi.
notes: The book prints no comma after `tu` in `Quam oblationem tu Deus`, and no cross signs over the five adjectives, which the Roman rite marks. `adscriptam` with d, as printed.

latin: Qui pridie quam pateretur, accepit panem in sanctas ac venerabiles manus suas, et elevatis oculis in cœlum, ad te Deum Patrem suum omnipotentem: tibi gratias agens, benedixit, fregit, deditque discipulis suis dicens: Accipite et manducate ex hoc omnes,
notes: Ends with a comma, the consecratory form following in the same paragraph as a separate block. `Accipite et manducate ex hoc omnes,` is NOT set in small capitals in the Latin column, where the corresponding English is; the Latin's capitals begin at the form itself. `cœlum` with the oe-ligature.

latin: HOC EST ENIM CORPUS MEUM.
notes: Set in small capitals in the Latin column and given here in capitals, as the sibling English row gives its own. The printing adds nothing after `MEUM.`: there is no counterpart to the postconciliar `quod pro vobis tradetur`.

latin: Simili modo postquam cœnatum est, accipiens et hunc præclarum calicem in sanctas ac venerabiles manus suas, item tibi gratias agens benedixit, deditque discipulis suis dicens:
notes: Runs over the page break xxxv/xxxvi, breaking at `in sanctas ac venerabiles` / `manus suas`. `cœnatum` with the oe-ligature. The block ends at `dicens:`, the small capitals of the form beginning with `ACCIPITE` in the next block.

latin: ACCIPITE ET BIBITE EX EO OMNES, HIC EST ENIM CALIX SANGUINIS MEI NOVI ET ÆTERNI TESTAMENTI: MYSTERIUM FIDEI: QUI PRO VOBIS ET PRO MULTIS EFFUNDETUR IN REMISSIONEM PECCATORUM.
notes: Set in small capitals beginning at `ACCIPITE`, so the extent of the capitals differs from the form over the bread, which begins at `HOC`; both are given here in capitals. `MYSTERIUM FIDEI` stands INSIDE the form. `ÆTERNI` with the ae-ligature.

latin: Hæc quotiescumque feceritis, in mei memoriam facietis.
notes: Printed as a separate paragraph after the form and not in small capitals. `Hæc` with the ae-ligature.

latin: Unde et memores, Domine, nos servi tui, sed et plebs tua sancta ejusdem Christi Filii tui, Domini nostri, tam beatæ passionis, necnon et ab inferis, Resurrectionis, sed et in Cœlos gloriosæ ascensionis, offerimus præclaræ Majestati tuæ, de tuis donis ac datis, Hostiam puram, Hostiam sanctam, Hostiam immaculatam, panem sanctum vitæ æternæ, et Calicem salutis perpetuæ.
notes: `Cœlos` capitalised and with the oe-ligature. No cross signs are printed over `Hostiam ... Calicem`.

latin: Supra quæ propitio ac sereno vultu respicere digneris, et accepta habere, sicuti accepta habere dignatus es munera pueri tui justi Abel, et sacrificium Patriarchæ nostri Abrahæ; et quod tibi obtulit summus sacerdos tuus Melchisedech, sanctum sacrificium, immaculatam Hostiam.
notes: Runs over the page break xxxvi/xxxvii, breaking at `respicere` / `digneris`. Heavy inking at the left edge of the Latin column of xxxvii damages the first letters of `habere` twice, of `sacerdos` and of `Melchisedech` at the line turn `Melchise-` / `dech`; every one is read from the surviving strokes on the leaf and none is repaired from another book.

latin: Supplices te rogamus, omnipotens Deus, jube hæc præferri per manus sancti angeli tui in sublime altare tuum, in conspectu divinæ Majestatis tuæ, ut quotquot ex hac altaris participatione, sacro-sanctum Filii tui corpus et sanguinem sumpserimus, omni benedictione cælesti et gratia repleamur. Per eumdem Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.
notes: `sacro-sanctum` is printed with its own hyphen, over and above the line-break hyphen after `sa-`. `corpus` and `sanguinem` lower-case here, where seq 11 sets `Corpus et Sanguis` with capitals. The book prints `cælesti` with the ae-ligature here, though it sets `cœlum`, `cœlis` and `Cœlos` with the oe-ligature elsewhere in this Canon; both are transcribed as printed and neither is harmonised. `Amen.` italic.

latin: Memento etiam, Domine, famulorum famularumque tuarum N. et N. qui nos præcesserunt cum signo Fidei, et dormiunt in somno pacis.
notes: `Fidei` capitalised as printed.

latin: Ipsis, Domine, et omnibus in Christo quiescentibus, locum refrigerii, lucis et pacis, ut indulgeas deprecamur: per eumdem Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.
notes: Runs over the page break xxxvii/xxxviii, breaking at `in Christo quies-` / `centibus`; the printed page and leaf given here are those of the block's greater part, as the sibling English row gives them. `per` lower-case in the conclusion, as printed. `Amen.` italic.

latin: Nobis quoque peccatoribus famulis tuis de multitudine miserationum tuarum sperantibus, partem aliquam et societatem donare digneris, cum tuis sanctis apostolis et martyribus; cum Joanne, Stephano, Matthia, Barnaba, Ignatio, Alexandro, Marcellino, Petro, Felicitate, Perpetua, Agatha, Lucia, Agnete, Cæcilia, Anastasia, et omnibus sanctis tuis: intra quorum nos consortium, non æstimator meriti, sed veniæ, quæsumus largitor admitte. Per Christum Dominum nostrum.
notes: `Cæcilia` and `æstimator` with the ae-ligature.

latin: Per quem hæc omnia, Domine, semper bona ereas, sanctificas, vivificas, benedicis, et præstas nobis.
notes: The Latin column misprints `ereas` for `creas`: the first letter carries the crossbar of an e and is not a c, read at 250 per cent on leaf n48. Transcribed as printed and not corrected. No cross signs are printed over the three verbs.

latin: Per ipsum, et cum ipso, et in ipso, est tibi Deo Patri omnipotenti, in unitate Spiritus Sancti, omnis honor et gloria.
notes: No cross signs are printed in this block, which the Roman rite marks five times.

latin: P. Per omnia sæcula sæculorum. R. Amen.
notes: The first two lines of xxxix, closing the Canon. Here `sæcula sæculorum` is set unbroken, where the same versicle at the foot of xxvii prints a full stop after `sæcula`. `Amen.` italic.
